groups.title: Optative meaning and time
groups.writingJob: Use the optative for wishes and hopes, preserve its two ordinary tenses, and enforce the special borrowed future and preterit uses.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through wish, hope, regret, disillusionment, and insisted-future readings.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses mood and tense; the application supplies the licensed form, meaning, and required preterit-optative antecessive ō.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Mood, Tense, and the existing antecessive behavior; do not add duplicate optative-time controls.
groups.derivedCueJob: Name the selected optative time and explain when its form is borrowed from the indicative.
groups.proposal: Make optative time a real grammatical choice while deriving its form and interpretation from Andrews.

groups.title: Building optative VNCs
groups.writingJob: Build nonpast and past optatives from the imperfective stem with their second-person, plural-number, and Class C or D realizations.
groups.readingJob: Help the reader identify which parts of an optative form make it distinctive.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the stem, participant, mood, and tense; the application chooses the imperfective stem, person morph, number dyad, and class-conditioned vowel.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not expose automatic x or xi, c-ān, stem truncation, vowel length, or slot placement as user choices.
groups.derivedCueJob: Mark the automatically selected optative person, number, tense, and predicate-stem contributions.
groups.proposal: Keep optative formation automatic and class-sensitive on the normal VNC path.

groups.title: Distinguishing optative and indicative forms
groups.writingJob: Preserve the form contrasts that distinguish optatives and require introductory particles where form alone cannot identify first- or third-person optatives.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through forms that are distinct, forms that are ambiguous, and the sentence clues that resolve them.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended mood and participant; the application realizes distinctive morphology and enforces the required sentence context.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Mood, Subject, and Particles; do not ask the user to label a form as morphologically ambiguous.
groups.derivedCueJob: Show whether morphology alone distinguishes the optative or whether the surrounding sentence does the work.
groups.proposal: Let morphology distinguish what it can and use licensed sentence context for the remaining ambiguity.

groups.title: Wish sentences
groups.writingJob: Build licensed wish sentences with their introductory particles, time meanings, and intensifying particles.
groups.readingJob: Guide open, contrary-to-fact, past-regret, and intensified wish readings.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended wish and available particles; the application orders them and enforces their meaning and compatibility.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Mood, Tense, Particles, and sentence choices; do not expose formula slots.
groups.proposal: Compose wishes from genuine choices through one optative sentence path.

groups.title: Negative wishes
groups.writingJob: Turn a licensed wish negative with the required ca structure and correct scope.
groups.readingJob: Guide the reader through negative wish meaning and particle scope.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses negative polarity; the application supplies and positions the licensed negative structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Polarity and Particles; do not expose raw ca placement.
groups.proposal: Make negative wishes a grammatical transformation rather than manual particle assembly.

groups.title: Commands and exhortations
groups.writingJob: Use optative VNCs as commands or exhortations according to participant and sentence context.
groups.readingJob: Guide command and exhortation force without inventing a separate imperative mood.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses sentence purpose and participant; the application keeps the grammatical mood optative and supplies the required context.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add an imperative mood; reuse Mood, Subject, sentence purpose, and Particles.
groups.proposal: Build commands and exhortations from the optative system Andrews describes.

groups.title: Second-person commands
groups.writingJob: Build direct second-person commands with the licensed optional introductory material.
groups.readingJob: Recognize a direct command from its second-person optative shape and context.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses second person and command use; the application realizes the optative command.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Subject, Mood, sentence purpose, and Particles.
groups.proposal: Keep direct commands inside the common optative sentence system.

groups.title: Third-person commands
groups.writingJob: Build third-person commands with their required introductory particle.
groups.readingJob: Use the introductory particle and context to identify indirect command force.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses third person and command use; the application requires and places the introductory particle.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Subject, Mood, sentence purpose, and Particles.
groups.proposal: Enforce the sentence context required for third-person commands.

groups.title: First-person exhortations
groups.writingJob: Build first-person exhortations with their required introductory particle and licensed strengthening.
groups.readingJob: Use participant and particle context to identify exhortation force.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses first person and exhortation use; the application supplies the licensed structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Subject, Mood, sentence purpose, and Particles.
groups.proposal: Enforce the sentence context required for first-person exhortations.

groups.title: Future commands
groups.writingJob: Use a future indicative form with optative command use when the commanded event is explicitly future.
groups.readingJob: Distinguish future command use from an ordinary future statement.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses future command meaning; the application borrows the future form and preserves command context.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Tense, sentence purpose, and Particles; do not add a second future-form control.
groups.proposal: Build future commands through the borrowed-form rule.

groups.title: Negative commands
groups.writingJob: Build negative commands and prohibitions with their licensed negative transformation and time behavior.
groups.readingJob: Guide prohibition force, scope, and the difference between immediate and future negative commands.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses command use, polarity, and time; the application supplies the negative command structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse sentence purpose, Polarity, Tense, and Particles.
groups.proposal: Make prohibition a normal grammatical transformation of the command path.
